title: Attachments keep binaries out of the operation log: state holds an opaque attachment://v1:<sha256> ref
content:
`@powerhousedao/reactor-attachments` exists to keep large binaries out of the action and operation pipeline. Instead of a base64 `data` string riding inside an action — and therefore inside the immutable operation log, and therefore across every sync channel forever — document state holds an opaque ref of the form `attachment://v1:<sha256>`, while the bytes flow through a separate `IAttachmentService`. Storage is content-addressed, so identical uploads dedupe to the same ref.

The integration surface with document models is a **single GraphQL scalar**, `AttachmentRef`:

```graphql
scalar AttachmentRef

input SetAgentImageInput { attachment: AttachmentRef! }
type AgentInfo { attachment: AttachmentRef }
```

Codegen emits a branded TypeScript string type (`` `attachment://v${number}:${string}` ``) plus a Zod validator enforcing the ref protocol. The reducer stores the value verbatim — there are no special "attach" actions and no attachment-aware reducer logic:

```typescript
setAgentImageOperation(state, action) {
  state.agent.attachment = action.input.attachment; // AttachmentRef
}
```

This is the architectural payoff: the document model never sees storage configuration, credentials, or transfer mechanics. The same model works whether Switchboard proxies bytes from the filesystem backend or the S3 backend transfers them directly via presigned URLs.

Reach for it whenever a field would otherwise be a base64 string or a long data URI — editor file/image uploads, avatars, any binary that must round-trip through sync or GraphQL. Keep small, fixed-length, non-binary values (short strings, numbers, JSON blobs) inline.

Two behaviors worth knowing before you rely on refs. `get(ref)` succeeds for any ref whose bytes are available and transparently re-fetches through the transport if they were evicted from local storage. But a hash-first ref can be **pending** — reserved, with state already referencing it, bytes not yet uploaded. In that window `get()` throws `AttachmentPending` while `stat()` succeeds and returns `status: "pending"` with the declared `sizeBytes` and `expiresAtUtc`. `AttachmentPending` is deliberately not a subclass of `AttachmentNotFound`: pending means "retry later", not "unknown".

Refs should be treated as opaque outside the service; `parseRef`/`createRef` are exported but are for tests and debugging tooling.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/09-AttachmentService.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
